115	## 5. Product contract
116	
117	### 5.1 Structural registration admission
118	
119	Add one process-owned `RegistrationService` admission budget with maximum 103.
120	It has no wait queue.
121	
122	- Validate input shape and `sourceContext(rawSource)` synchronously first,
123	  preserving `AUTH_INPUT_INVALID` behavior and consuming no admission budget for
124	  invalid input or invalid source context.
125	- Acquire synchronously after that validation and before the first repository await,
126	  limiter lookup, audit/password KDF, mail reservation, token mint, or mutation.
127	- Request 104 receives the existing opaque retryable `AUTH_MAIL_BUSY` envelope
128	  and still traverses the existing 600 ms registration response clamp.
129	- The refusal performs no repository, limiter, audit KDF, password KDF, mail
130	  reservation, token mint, account mutation, send, or delivery audit. Emit only
131	  the existing opaque bounded capacity signal; never address/source material.
132	- Counter never exceeds 103 or underflows. Releasing a slot allows a later new
133	  request; requests refused at 104 are not queued by this gate.
134	
135	Use one idempotent release closure. The token covers rate-limit work, shared
136	mail reservation, hashing, provisioning, response clamp, permit activation and
137	ownership transfer. Release only in an outermost `finally`, after the existing
138	handoff block has either:
139	
140	- transferred successful postwork to `dispatchVerification`, or
141	- transferred failed/no-postwork reservation ownership to the bounded
142	  reservation-hold continuation.
143	
144	Do not hold admission through actual transport or delivery audit after a
145	continuation owns that work. Do not release at commit, response creation, clamp
146	entry, or before handoff. When reservation ownership continues asynchronously
147	after a hash/audit failure, transfer the idempotent admission release atomically
148	out of the local `finally` and into exactly one reservation continuation:
149	
150	- on reservation grant, the continuation must first call
151	  `dispatchMailReservationHold` synchronously so the hold promise is registered
152	  in `pendingMailDispatches`; only after that registration may it release the
153	  admission token, and it must not await the 5.1-second hold before releasing;
154	- on reservation rejection, the continuation releases the admission token in
155	  its own `finally`;
156	- normal success and synchronous provision/failure paths keep local ownership
157	  and release only after their dispatch/handoff block finishes.
158	
159	The local and continuation owners must be mutually exclusive. Every
160	rejection/cancellation path settles exactly once with no unhandled promise.
161	
162	### 5.2 Route-specific deadline
163	
164	Make the shared reservation method accept an explicit named wait deadline.
165	Defaults and resend remain 18,000 ms. Registration alone passes 28,000 ms.
166	
167	- Deadline timer removes the exact waiter object, clears itself on handoff, and
168	  leaves no queue node or retained request after settlement.
169	- A 28-second registration timeout remains typed `AUTH_MAIL_BUSY`, traverses
170	  the same clamp, cancels/clears unstarted password work and transfers any
171	  already-owned work safely.
172	- Do not change cadence 45 ms, resend cadence 60 ms, 32 active permits, 96
173	  shared waiters, 5.1/5.7-second reservations, 600 ms clamp, 5-second transport
174	  bound, KDF parameters, pool counts/caps/timeouts, or queue arbitration.
175	
176	### 5.3 Admission shutdown/drain
177	
178	Add an idempotent admission close-and-drain state:
179	
180	- once closing begins, reject new registration admissions with a generic typed
181	  retryable failure;
182	- await the exact transition to zero admitted registrations;
183	- repeated/concurrent drains join one promise and do not underflow or hang;
184	- the real API shutdown order is admission drain, mail-dispatch drain,
185	  rate-limit/refusal-audit drain, audit hasher close, then Argon pool close;
186	- no registration may enqueue mail/audit work after the corresponding drain has
187	  returned.
188	
189	The admission drain is a fail-closed join of in-flight ownership. Do not claim a
190	whole-request bound that does not exist: repository/transaction awaits have no
191	request-wide cancellation deadline, and the Argon worker timeout begins only
192	at dispatch. Rework7 must not invent DB/request cancellation semantics. T3 (or
193	the deployment shutdown owner) remains responsible for any outer process-level
194	shutdown budget and escalation policy.
195	
196	### 5.4 Policy decision version 3
197	
198	Publish a new versioned decision beside preserved v1/v2 evidence. The durable
199	shape may be minimally refactored, but all of these facts must be typed and
200	machine-readable:
201	
202	- structural maximum concurrent registrations = 103;
203	- registration mail-permit wait deadline = 28,000 ms;
204	- shared/resend wait deadline = 18,000 ms;
205	- registration cadence = 45 ms, status provisional/recalibration-pending;
206	- scope = healthy MTA, target host, initially empty shared dispatcher,
207	  register-only simultaneous burst;
208	- mixed register/resend availability is not guaranteed by this decision;
209	- v2 N*=3, 430 ms, 35 ms and measured 103 remain historical observations but
210	  status is superseded/contradicted by unchanged-code RED evidence;
211	- current positive N* = none/null; historical N*=2 is not a fallback;
212	- diagnostic repeats and 20,922.9/21,902.2/20,942.1 ms maxima;
213	- retention disclosure: at most 103 admitted registration frames; at most 96
214	  shared mail-queue waiters; a queued registration frame may retain validated
215	  email, recovery email, password and source context for at most 28 seconds;
216	  no raw verification token is minted before mail grant.
217	
218	Replace code/comments/tests that call 103 a measured exact capacity with the
219	structural admission-cap meaning. Do not delete or rewrite the underlying v1/v2
220	measurement arrays; retain them as history with honest status.
221	
222	## 6. Mandatory RED-first tests
223	
224	Before product edits, add non-vacuous tests and run the focused RED set. Preserve
225	raw output/status and exact reasons. Required mechanisms:
226	
227	1. barrier-controlled valid requests prove 100 and 103 are admitted, request
228	   104 is refused synchronously, and 128/160 never exceed 103;
229	   invalid input and invalid source context consume no admission slot;
230	2. the 104th request invokes zero repository, limiter, password/audit KDF, mail
231	   reservation, token, mutation, send or audit operations;
232	3. 104th refusal still completes only after the 600 ms clamp and is
233	   byte/status-identical across address-existence arms;
234	4. exact-once release for success, duplicate, rate-limit refusal, immediate
235	   shared-queue full, 28-second timeout, hash failure before/after dispatch,
236	   audit failure, DB failure, clamp failure, handoff/continuation failure,
237	   cancellation and shutdown;
238	5. early release before clamp/handoff is caught; counter max/underflow and
239	   next-request admission are asserted;
240	6. registration timer is exactly 28 seconds while resend remains exactly 18;
241	7. exact waiter identity/timer cleanup, password clearing, no pregrant token,
242	   no unhandled rejection and no secret-bearing log;
243	8. admission drain prevents post-drain enqueue and proves the real shutdown
244	   ordering;
245	9. policy v3 is machine-readable, v2 is historical/contradicted, 45 ms is
246	   provisional and current N* is absent rather than silently falling back;
247	10. real PostgreSQL healthy-MTA bursts 100/103/104/128/160 produce structural
248	    successes 100/103/103/103/103, matching commits and sends, with every excess
249	    request typed busy and no unexpected error.
250	
251	Use deterministic barriers for lifecycle logic; do not make a 28-second unit
252	test sleep in wall time. Real PostgreSQL timing evidence remains foreground and
253	fresh-process.
254	
255	## 7. GREEN, calibration and regression gates
256	
257	On stable candidate bytes, run in the foreground with complete receipts:
258	
259	1. focused unit registration tests for admission/deadline/drain;
260	2. focused architecture shutdown/pool ownership tests;
261	3. real PostgreSQL Rework7 admission/capacity tests;
262	4. three consecutive fresh exact-candidate healthy-MTA bursts proving 100 and
263	   the structural cap 103 under the approved scope;
264	5. exactly one preconditioned full registration-file invocation, after the
265	   focused gates and three fresh burst repeats, preserving its natural file
266	   order and one shared process-owned pool:
267	
268	   ```text
269	   node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts
270	   ```
271	
272	   Record complete output/status durably and do not rerun it on failure. No
273	   substitute or "bounded equivalent" is allowed without a V-approved packet
274	   amendment recorded on Kanban;
275	6. existing resend 18-second deadline/equal-arm test;
276	7. deep-queue, slow-transport, audit-KDF, heap/retention, shutdown/drain,
277	   timing-opacity/AUC/classifier and T9 deadlock regressions;
278	8. `pnpm typecheck`;
279	9. `pnpm lint`;
280	10. `git diff --check`.
281	
282	N*=3 is not a Rework7 GREEN claim. Preserve its failing evidence and policy
283	supersession. Do not weaken existing privacy thresholds, 600/100/250 ms limits,
284	or deadlock gates to compensate. The repository-wide `pnpm test` remains
285	reserved for a later fresh final-custody seat after dual Sol approval.
286	
287	## 8. VR-10 mutation requirements
288	
289	At minimum, independently prove RED and exact restore for mutants that:
290	
291	- remove/raise the 103 cap;
292	- acquire after the first repository await;
293	- release at commit or before clamp/handoff;
294	- release before an asynchronously granted reservation hold is synchronously
295	  registered in `pendingMailDispatches`;
296	- retain admission through the actual 5.1-second reservation hold after that
297	  hold has been registered;
298	- make release non-idempotent;
299	- use 18 seconds for registration;
300	- use 28 seconds for resend;
301	- leave a timed-out waiter/password retained;
302	- reorder shutdown so mail drain precedes admission drain;
303	- keep v2 marked CURRENT or publish a positive current N*;
304	- derive capacity from observed completion rather than the structural counter.
305	
306	A zero-test match, generic compiler failure, timeout, survivor, missing receipt
307	or non-byte-identical restore is a hard stop.
308	
309	## 9. Handoff and hard stops
310	
311	Finish `REWORK READY FOR PEER REVIEW` only when all authorized focused/static
312	gates and mutants are green/RED as required, final HEAD/index/custody is exact,
313	and the diff is limited to the six allowed files. Otherwise finish

Do NOT `boards switch` (global pointer shared with other missions).

- **codex exec resume can HANG ON EXIT after completing its work** (verified 2026-08-22): seat posted its full handoff to the Kanban ticket at 11:11 then sat at 0.0%% CPU for 81 min with no further output. Diagnose by reading the BOARD not the log — the log can lag the final board write. Cross-probe the relay with a tiny codex exec first; if it answers, the backend is fine and only that session is wedged. Killing it is safe once the handoff is durable; the session id stays resumable.
- **hermes --yolo -z BUFFERS stdout until completion** (verified 2026-08-21): a silent tee log is NOT a hang. Liveness-check via read-only sqlite: `sqlite3 -readonly ~/.hermes/state.db "SELECT message_count,tool_call_count,input_tokens FROM sessions ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 5;"` — counters advancing = working. Alarm-killed probes leave orphan RUNNING rows (harmless). Three concurrent hermes one-shots on the gpt-5.6-sol relay run slow but do progress.
- Keep big prompts off argv (repo lesson, commit fc05bce): pass a short `/goal` pointer prompt referencing a goal-packet file the agent reads itself.
- Mission scaffold pattern used: `apps/dialectical-engine/docs/missions/<date>-<slug>/` with `00-intake-H0.md`, `goal-packets/`, `research/`, `logs/`, `upstream/`.

import type { Pool } from "pg";
import { z } from "zod";
import { TypedDomainError } from "@debateai/kernel";

export const AUTH_POLICY_ROW_KEYS = [
  "passwordPolicy", "auditSourceIpKdfPolicy", "verificationPolicy", "rateLimitPolicy", "channelPolicy"
] as const;

const passwordPolicySchema = z.object({
  kind: z.literal("PASSWORD_POLICY"),
  minimum_length: z.literal(8),
  composition_rules: z.literal(false),
  forced_rotation: z.literal(false),
  // Finite upper bounds only. Every lower bound and every shipped value is
  // unchanged; these maxima exist so a syntactically valid but hostile register
  // row cannot defeat the worker pool's resource bound by demanding, say, a
  // multi-gibibyte Argon2 allocation per job. The maxima sit at the currently
  // supported ceiling, so no deployed policy value moves.
  argon2id: z.object({
    memory_cost_kib: z.number().int().min(19_456).max(262_144),
    time_cost: z.number().int().min(2).max(10),
    parallelism: z.number().int().positive().max(4),
    hash_length: z.number().int().min(32).max(64)
  }).strict()
}).strict();

const auditSourceIpKdfPolicySchema = z.object({
  kind: z.literal("AUDIT_SOURCE_IP_KDF_POLICY"),
  algorithm: z.literal("argon2id"),
  memory_cost_kib: z.number().int().min(19_456).max(262_144),
  iterations: z.number().int().min(2).max(10),
  // Bounded for the same reason as the password KDF above; the shipped value
  // (1) and every other audit KDF value are unchanged.
  parallelism: z.number().int().positive().max(4),
  hash_length: z.literal(32)
}).strict();

const verificationPolicySchema = z.object({
  kind: z.literal("VERIFICATION_POLICY"),
  token_ttl_ms: z.number().int().positive().max(24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000),
  resend_cooldown_ms: z.number().int().positive(),
  outbound_send_window_ms: z.literal(60 * 60_000),
  outbound_send_max: z.literal(3),

    mechanism: z.literal("per_row_last_sent_timestamp_minimum_spacing"),
    minimum_spacing_ms: z.literal(20 * 60_000)
  }).strict(),
  verification_credentials: z.object({
    storage: z.literal("HASH_ONLY_APPEND_ONLY_LEDGER"),
    validity: z.literal("EACH_MAILED_TOKEN_UNTIL_OWN_EXPIRY_OR_ACCOUNT_ACTIVATION"),
    maximum_live_hashes_per_account: z.literal(73),
    pruning: z.literal("ON_RESEND_DELETE_EXPIRED"),
    leaked_token_tradeoff: z.string().regex(/cannot.*revoke.*resend/i)

  enumeration_response_floor_ms: z.number().int().positive(),
  enumeration_tolerance_ms: z.number().int().positive()
}).strict();

const routeLimitSchema = z.object({
  window_ms: z.number().int().positive(),
  admission_per_source: z.number().int().positive(),
  per_ip: z.number().int().positive(),

        "200000": z.number().int().nonnegative(),

        "800000": z.number().int().nonnegative()

  routes: z.object({

      count_cap: z.literal(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER),
      maximum_retained_aggregates: z.literal(1)
    }).strict(),

      ruled_hash_and_provisioning_upper_bound_ms: z.number().int().positive(),

        }).strict(),

export function authPolicyFromRegisterRows(rows: readonly AuthPolicyRegisterRow[]): AuthPolicy {
  const byKey = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.rowKey, row]));
  for (const key of AUTH_POLICY_ROW_KEYS) {
    const row = byKey.get(key);
    if (row === undefined || row.sourceRef.trim() === "") {
      throw new TypedDomainError("AUTH_POLICY_UNRESOLVED", `Missing ruled ${key}`);
    }
  }
  const password = passwordPolicySchema.safeParse(byKey.get("passwordPolicy")!.value);
  const auditSourceIpKdf = auditSourceIpKdfPolicySchema.safeParse(
    byKey.get("auditSourceIpKdfPolicy")!.value
  );
  const verification = verificationPolicySchema.safeParse(byKey.get("verificationPolicy")!.value);
  const rateLimits = rateLimitPolicySchema.safeParse(byKey.get("rateLimitPolicy")!.value);
  const channel = channelPolicySchema.safeParse(byKey.get("channelPolicy")!.value);
  if (!password.success || !auditSourceIpKdf.success || !verification.success
    || !rateLimits.success || !channel.success) {
    throw new TypedDomainError("AUTH_POLICY_INVALID", "An authentication register row violates its ruled member type");
  }
  const routePolicy = (route: keyof typeof rateLimits.data.routes): AuthRouteLimit => Object.freeze({
    windowMs: rateLimits.data.routes[route].window_ms,
    admissionPerSource: rateLimits.data.routes[route].admission_per_source
  });
  if (verification.success
    && verification.data.resend_cooldown_ms * verification.data.outbound_send_max
      < verification.data.outbound_send_window_ms) {
    throw new TypedDomainError(
      "AUTH_POLICY_INVALID",
      "Verification cooldown does not enforce the outbound send ceiling"
    );
  }
  if (rateLimits.success
    && rateLimits.data.bucket_capacity !== rateLimits.data.sketch_design.slots_per_route) {
    throw new TypedDomainError("AUTH_POLICY_INVALID", "Rate-limit capacity contradicts sketch design");
  }
  const dispatch = channel.data.verification_dispatch;
  const derivedPreTransportBudgetMs = verification.data.enumeration_response_floor_ms
    + verification.data.enumeration_tolerance_ms;
  const derivedMinimumReservationMs = derivedPreTransportBudgetMs
    + channel.data.transport_timeout_ms + dispatch.handoff_scheduler_tolerance_ms;
  const derivedRegistrationMinimumReservationMs = channel.data.transport_timeout_ms
    + dispatch.handoff_scheduler_tolerance_ms;
  const absorption = dispatch.registration_clamp_absorption;
  const safetyAdjustedWorkMs = Math.ceil(
    absorption.measured_hash_and_provisioning_max_ms
      * absorption.measurement_safety_percent / 100 / 10
  ) * 10;
  const derivedClampHeadroomMs = derivedPreTransportBudgetMs - (
    absorption.ruled_hash_and_provisioning_upper_bound_ms
      + absorption.maximum_unsaturated_concurrency
        * dispatch.registration_activation_spacing_ms
  );
  if (dispatch.pre_transport_work_budget_ms !== derivedPreTransportBudgetMs
    || dispatch.no_send_equal_transport_work_ms !== channel.data.transport_timeout_ms
    || dispatch.minimum_reservation_ms !== derivedMinimumReservationMs
    || dispatch.registration_minimum_reservation_ms
      !== derivedRegistrationMinimumReservationMs
    || dispatch.maximum_concurrent_registration_hashes > dispatch.maximum_concurrent
    || dispatch.activation_spacing_ms * dispatch.maximum_concurrent
      > dispatch.minimum_reservation_ms
    || absorption.measurement_safety_percent !== 110
    || absorption.ruled_hash_and_provisioning_upper_bound_ms !== safetyAdjustedWorkMs
    || absorption.response_clamp_ms !== derivedPreTransportBudgetMs
    || absorption.binding_headroom_ms !== derivedClampHeadroomMs
    || derivedClampHeadroomMs <= 0
    || absorption.first_measured_unabsorbed_concurrency
      !== absorption.maximum_unsaturated_concurrency + 1) {
    throw new TypedDomainError(
      "AUTH_POLICY_INVALID",
      "Mail reservation derivation contradicts verification or transport policy"
    );
  }
  // The CURRENT decision is derived by exactly the same arithmetic as the sealed
  // one, from its own measurement, so publishing a new version can never smuggle
  // in an unratified safety factor, upper bound or headroom.
  const current = dispatch.current_registration_clamp_absorption;
  const currentSafetyAdjustedWorkMs = Math.ceil(
    current.measured_hash_and_provisioning_max_ms
      * current.measurement_safety_percent / 100 / 10
  ) * 10;
  const currentClampHeadroomMs = derivedPreTransportBudgetMs - (
    current.ruled_hash_and_provisioning_upper_bound_ms
      + current.maximum_unsaturated_concurrency * dispatch.registration_activation_spacing_ms
  );
  const capacity = current.measured_accepted_request_capacity;
  if (current.measurement_safety_percent !== absorption.measurement_safety_percent
    || current.ruled_hash_and_provisioning_upper_bound_ms !== currentSafetyAdjustedWorkMs
    || current.response_clamp_ms !== derivedPreTransportBudgetMs
    || current.binding_headroom_ms !== currentClampHeadroomMs
    || currentClampHeadroomMs <= 0
    || current.first_measured_unabsorbed_concurrency
      !== current.maximum_unsaturated_concurrency + 1
    // The cadence is explicitly UNCHANGED by this decision.
    || current.registration_activation_spacing_ms !== dispatch.registration_activation_spacing_ms
    // A ratified N* may never exceed the WORST repeat's raw absorbed maximum.
    // With raw maxima [4,4,3] this is what structurally forbids claiming N*=4.
    || current.maximum_unsaturated_concurrency
      > Math.min(...current.evidence.raw_maximum_absorbed_concurrency_per_repeat)
    // ...and the ratified N must be supported by a positive headroom in EVERY
    // repeat, not merely on average.
    || current.evidence.n3_clamp_headroom_tenths_ms.some((headroom) => headroom <= 0)
    || current.maximum_unsaturated_concurrency !== 3
    // The published capacity is the one every repeat actually measured.
    || current.evidence.burst_128_accepted_per_repeat.some((accepted) => accepted !== capacity)
    || current.evidence.burst_160_accepted_per_repeat.some((accepted) => accepted !== capacity)
    // The sealed decision must survive this publication byte-for-byte.
    || absorption.maximum_unsaturated_concurrency !== 2
    || absorption.ruled_hash_and_provisioning_upper_bound_ms !== 480
    || absorption.binding_headroom_ms !== 30) {
    throw new TypedDomainError(
      "AUTH_POLICY_INVALID",
      "Current clamp-absorption decision contradicts its measured evidence or the sealed decision"
    );

      iterations: auditSourceIpKdf.data.iterations,
      parallelism: auditSourceIpKdf.data.parallelism,
      hashLength: auditSourceIpKdf.data.hash_length
    }),
    verification: Object.freeze({
      tokenTtlMs: verification.data.token_ttl_ms,
      resendCooldownMs: verification.data.resend_cooldown_ms,
      outboundSendWindowMs: verification.data.outbound_send_window_ms,
      outboundSendMax: verification.data.outbound_send_max,
      enumerationResponseFloorMs: verification.data.enumeration_response_floor_ms,
      enumerationToleranceMs: verification.data.enumeration_tolerance_ms
    }),
    rateLimits: Object.freeze({
      register: routePolicy("register"),
      verify: routePolicy("verify"),
      resend: routePolicy("resend")
    }),
    rateLimitBucketCapacity: rateLimits.data.bucket_capacity,
    rateLimitRefusalAuditIntervalMs: rateLimits.data.refusal_audit_interval_ms,
    channel: Object.freeze({
      transport: channel.data.transport,
      senderLocalPart: channel.data.sender_local_part,
      transportTimeoutMs: channel.data.transport_timeout_ms,
      spamNotice: channel.data.spam_notice,
      maxConcurrentVerificationDispatches: channel.data.verification_dispatch.maximum_concurrent,
      maxQueuedVerificationDispatches: channel.data.verification_dispatch.queue_capacity,
      maxConcurrentRegistrationHashes:
        channel.data.verification_dispatch.maximum_concurrent_registration_hashes,
      mailDispatchActivationSpacingMs:
        channel.data.verification_dispatch.activation_spacing_ms,
      registrationMailDispatchActivationSpacingMs:

export async function readAuthPolicy(pool: Pool, registerVersion: number): Promise<AuthPolicy> {
  if (!Number.isInteger(registerVersion) || registerVersion < 1) {
    throw new TypeError("A positive register version is required for auth policy");
  }
  const result = await pool.query<{ row_key: string; value_json: unknown; source_ref: string }>(`
    SELECT row_key,value_json,source_ref FROM register.register_row
    WHERE register_version=$1 AND row_key=ANY($2::text[])
  `, [registerVersion, AUTH_POLICY_ROW_KEYS]);
  return authPolicyFromRegisterRows(result.rows.map((row) => ({
    rowKey: row.row_key as AuthPolicyRegisterRow["rowKey"],
    value: row.value_json as Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>,
    sourceRef: row.source_ref
  })));
}
